name: Hyaluronic acid instilled into the bladder
short: Bladder instillation data only. Small studies: urine retention and a urinary infection (2 events in 32 patients), mild blood in urine (2 of 30); events as frequent as with interferon.
text: The data below are for hyaluronic acid instilled into the bladder (intravesical instillation, a clinic treatment); none of the cited sources covers hyaluronic acid taken by mouth or given by other routes. In a double-masked randomised trial in 52 women with interstitial cystitis comparing bladder instillations of interferon or hyaluronic acid, the frequencies of adverse events were similar between the groups, and 1 patient stopped hyaluronic acid because of poor effectiveness. In a randomised comparison with chondroitin sulfate instillation (21 patients per group) in bladder pain syndrome/interstitial cystitis, no severe adverse effects were reported. In a series of 32 patients with chronic bladder conditions (radiation cystitis, bladder pain syndrome/interstitial cystitis or recurrent cystitis), all tolerated the instillations, and 2 adverse effects were recorded: a urinary tract infection and acute urine retention. In a prospective study of 30 people with radiation-induced cystitis given a high-molecular-weight hyaluronate, two treatment-related adverse events (6.6%) were reported, both grade 1 blood in the urine, and in a randomised trial in 36 patients with radiation-induced haemorrhagic cystitis comparing instillation with hyperbaric oxygen, all completed the study and no obvious side effects of hyaluronic acid were recorded. A 2025 review of 8 studies (428 patients) from Taiwan in refractory interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome reports that no significant adverse events from the treatment were reported. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
